[1/4] Plan rejudge: re-score existing artifacts without a provider, preserve prior verdicts in schema-3 history, support multiple paths/strict/JSON

impact_assessment.why: Changing judge model or threshold currently forces a full re-render to refresh evidence, even though the audio already exists
impact_assessment.benefits: Existing tracks can be re-scored cheaply, prior verdicts remain auditable, and list/show keep reading the latest result
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new rejudge command and schema 3 history; dependency: none; concurrency: sequential atomic updates; state: muse.json rewritten in place with history
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate every artifact and audio before judging, build the judge once, write atomically per artifact, keep failures unchanged, test history/list/show and strict exits

impact_assessment.risks: contract: rejudge metadata settings only; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: muse.json settings/history
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use verdict fields, add a named-judge test, run the full suite and push
